subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the mnemonic 'MAD T-SHIRT' for the elements of music, what does the 'I' stand for?
questions.explain: In 'MAD T-SHIRT' the I stands for instrumentation, meaning the choice of instruments and voices used.

questions.q: Which Italian tempo term means 'fast and lively'?
questions.explain: Allegro means fast and lively, whereas adagio and largo are slow.

questions.q: What does the dynamic marking 'mezzo-forte' (mf) mean?
questions.explain: Mezzo-forte means moderately loud, sitting between piano and forte.

questions.q: Which term refers to the tone quality or 'colour' of a sound that lets you tell a flute from a violin?
questions.explain: Timbre, or sonority, is the characteristic tone colour that distinguishes one instrument or voice from another.

questions.q: In vocal technique, 'vibrato' is:
options: A slight, regular wavering of pitch to enrich the tone
questions.explain: Vibrato is a slight, regular variation in pitch that adds warmth to a sustained note.

questions.q: A sharp sign in front of a note does what?
options: Lowers the pitch by a semitone
Raises the pitch by a semitone
questions.explain: A sharp raises a note's pitch by one semitone.

questions.q: A triad in 'first inversion' has which note in the bass?
questions.explain: In first inversion the third of the chord is the lowest sounding note.

questions.q: 'Imitation' as a way of developing an idea means:
options: One part copies a melodic idea just stated by another part
questions.explain: Imitation is when one part copies a melodic idea introduced by another part.

questions.q: A 'pedal' (or pedal point) in texture is:
options: A sustained or repeated note, often in the bass, held under changing harmonies
questions.explain: A pedal is a held or repeated note, usually in the bass, that continues while harmonies change above it.

questions.q: When sequencing in a DAW, individual notes are often arranged on a:
questions.explain: In a DAW, notes are commonly entered and arranged on a piano roll along a track timeline.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using a metronome when practising a performance?
options: It helps you keep a steady, accurate tempo
questions.explain: A metronome sounds a steady beat, helping a performer keep an accurate and consistent tempo.

questions.q: 'Sight-reading' means:
options: Playing music you have not seen before, at first sight
questions.explain: Sight-reading is performing a piece of music you are seeing for the first time.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: The interval of an octave between two notes of the same letter name spans how many semitones?
questions.explain: An octave spans twelve semitones from one note to the next of the same name.

questions.q: When performing in an ensemble, watching a conductor or leader mainly helps players to:
options: Stay together in time and respond to changes
questions.explain: Following a conductor or leader keeps the ensemble together in time and unified in expression.

questions.q: What does 'a tempo' mean after a passage that has slowed down?
questions.explain: 'A tempo' instructs the performer to return to the original speed after a change.

questions.q: Which cadence ends on chord V, sounding unfinished?
questions.explain: An imperfect cadence ends on chord V and sounds incomplete.

questions.q: What does a 'coda' provide at the end of a composition?
options: A concluding section that rounds off the piece
questions.explain: A coda is a concluding section added to round off and finish a piece of music.

questions.q: A major triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A major triad stacks a major 3rd then a minor 3rd, giving a bright sound.

questions.q: A minim is worth how many crotchet beats?
questions.explain: A minim is worth two crotchet beats.

questions.q: In a DAW, 'automation' is most commonly used to:
options: Make settings like volume or panning change automatically over time
questions.explain: Automation lets parameters such as volume or panning change automatically across a track over time.

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.
